requirements.text: A ticket carries a level field with values ticket or epic; when no level is present the ticket reads as ticket without on-disk migration.
Setting level works identically through the CLI, MCP, and backend REST API.
An epic moves through three lifecycle states: Proposed then Approved then Implemented.

When a user sets phaseEpic to a ticket key, the system requires the target to exist, be an epic, and be in a usable state (Approved or Implemented); otherwise the write is rejected with an actionable error naming the target and remediation.
When a user moves an epic to Implemented while it has one or more non-terminal children, the system blocks the move and lists the blocking children; when all children are terminal the move succeeds.
The level field is queryable and filterable through the ticket list surface (e.g. ticket list level=epic).
Alias shorthand for level (e to epic, t to ticket) resolves consistently across CLI and MCP via the shared layer.
No migration: existing tickets without a level field read as ticket on read; no on-disk rewrite.
phaseEpic remains the child-to-epic link field; no epicId and no stored children array is introduced.
For the epic close guard, terminal statuses are Implemented, Rejected, and Partially Implemented; all other statuses count as non-terminal.
The epic close guard is scoped narrowly to epics moving to Implemented; free status movement is preserved for all non-epic tickets and for all other transitions.
Epics are never rendered as cards on the flat board; this is a documented divergence from designs/board-zai/design3-epics.md section 2 (board UI itself is MDT-206).

Level alias resolution lives in the shared layer (shared/services/ticket/attrResolver) so CLI, MCP, and any future consumer apply identical rules with no drift; mirrors the existing status alias precedent.
The backend OpenAPI documentation describes the new level field (derived from the zod schema plus property docs).
A phaseEpic value in a cross-project key format (e.g. ABC-012) is validated against the target project's ticket (must exist, be an epic, be usable).
Clearing phaseEpic on a ticket is always allowed regardless of the referenced epic's state.
An epic with zero children can be moved freely; the close guard only applies when children exist and are non-terminal.
Existing children already pointing at an epic are not retroactively rejected when that epic is moved back to Proposed; the reference guard applies to new writes only.
Reopening an epic from Implemented back to Approved is allowed; closes are not permanent.
Setting phaseEpic to a value that is not a ticket key (free text) succeeds unchanged; only ticket-key-shaped values are validated.
Setting phaseEpic to a ticket key whose target does not exist is rejected with a clear error.

The metadata-only CR list endpoint (GET /api/projects/:projectId/crs, served by getProjectCRsMetadata -> scanTicketMetadata -> normalizeTicketMetadata) preserves the level field: a ticket with level: epic returns level 'epic', and a legacy ticket without level returns 'ticket'. The metadata response must not include content.

scenarios.title: Ticket without explicit level reads as ticket
scenarios.given: A markdown ticket file with no level field in its frontmatter
scenarios.when: The ticket is parsed and normalized
scenarios.then: The resulting ticket has level equal to ticket with no on-disk rewrite

scenarios.title: Ticket with level epic round-trips through YAML
scenarios.given: A ticket whose frontmatter contains level: epic
scenarios.when: The ticket is written and re-read
scenarios.then: The level reads back as epic and the YAML contains the level key

scenarios.title: Setting level via CLI persists the field
scenarios.given: A ticket exists and a user runs the CLI attribute mutation with level=epic
scenarios.then: The shared service persists level and a subsequent get reads level epic

scenarios.title: Setting level via MCP update_cr_attrs persists the field
scenarios.given: A ticket exists and an MCP client calls update_cr_attrs with level=epic
scenarios.then: The shared service persists level and a get returns level epic

scenarios.title: Setting level via REST PATCH persists the field
scenarios.given: A ticket exists and a client PATCHes the cr endpoint with level=epic
scenarios.when: The server adapter forwards the update
scenarios.then: The shared service persists level and the response reflects level epic

scenarios.title: An epic moves Proposed to Approved to Implemented
scenarios.when: The user advances its status to Approved then Implemented
scenarios.then: Both transitions succeed and the status reads back accordingly

scenarios.title: Setting phaseEpic to a non-epic ticket key is rejected
scenarios.given: A target ticket exists with level ticket
scenarios.when: The user sets phaseEpic on a child to that target key
scenarios.then: The write is rejected with an error naming the target and stating it must be an epic

scenarios.title: Setting phaseEpic to a missing ticket key is rejected
scenarios.given: No ticket exists with the given key
scenarios.when: The user sets phaseEpic to that key
scenarios.then: The write is rejected with a clear error stating the target does not exist

scenarios.title: Setting phaseEpic to a Proposed epic is rejected
scenarios.given: The target ticket is an epic in Proposed status
scenarios.when: The user sets phaseEpic to that epic key
scenarios.then: The write is rejected stating the epic must be Approved first

scenarios.title: Setting phaseEpic to an Approved epic succeeds
scenarios.given: The target ticket is an epic in Approved status
scenarios.when: The user sets phaseEpic to that epic key

scenarios.title: Setting phaseEpic to an Implemented epic succeeds
scenarios.given: The target ticket is an epic in Implemented status
scenarios.when: The user sets phaseEpic to that epic key

scenarios.title: Setting phaseEpic to free non-key text succeeds unchanged
scenarios.given: The phaseEpic value is not ticket-key shaped
scenarios.when: The user sets phaseEpic to that free text
scenarios.then: The write succeeds with no target lookup

scenarios.title: Closing an epic with non-terminal children is blocked
scenarios.given: An epic has at least one child in a non-terminal status
scenarios.when: The user moves the epic to Implemented
scenarios.then: The move is rejected and the error lists the blocking children

scenarios.title: Closing an epic with all-terminal children succeeds
scenarios.given: An epic whose children are all in terminal statuses
scenarios.when: The user moves the epic to Implemented

scenarios.title: Non-epic tickets move to Implemented freely
scenarios.when: A ticket with level ticket has children or none
scenarios.then: The user moves it to Implemented	The move succeeds without the close guard applying

scenarios.title: Tickets can be listed and filtered by level
scenarios.given: Multiple tickets exist with mixed levels
scenarios.when: The user runs ticket list level=epic

scenarios.title: Alias shorthand resolves consistently
scenarios.given: A user supplies the shorthand e or t for the level field
scenarios.when: The alias is resolved through the shared resolver
scenarios.then: It canonicalizes to epic or ticket respectively across CLI and MCP

scenarios.title: Metadata list endpoint preserves level and excludes content
scenarios.given: A project with one ticket whose frontmatter has level: epic and one legacy ticket without a level field
scenarios.when: the Board consumer calls GET /api/projects/:projectId/crs (the metadata-only list path)
scenarios.then: the epic ticket returns level 'epic', the legacy ticket returns level 'ticket', and no item includes a content field

testPlans.title: Pure epic rules: ticket-key shape, usable epic state, close-terminal set, phaseEpic target resolution (all four outcomes), close guard with mixed/terminal children, structured error codes
domain-contracts: CRLevel enum shape, level on TicketSchema defaults/accepts/rejects, frontmatter schema, create/update input schemas, level in TICKET_UPDATE_ATTRS
shared normalizeTicket/normalizeTicketMetadata: level defaults to ticket when absent, preserves epic when present, round-trips through YAML serialization
shared TicketService: phaseEpic write validation rejects non-epic/missing/proposed targets, accepts approved/implemented/free-text, allows clear; createCR path same rules
shared attrResolver: LEVEL_ALIASES resolve e/t/canonical, resolveLevelToken throws on unknown, resolveAttrValue dispatches level
CLI: level token in ATTR_FIELDS, level in FILTER_FIELD_MAPPING, alias resolution routes through shared resolver
REST: PATCH forwards level (round-trip), create forwards level, EPIC_* errors map to 4xx with actionable messages, OpenAPI documents level
shared listCRs + CLI list: filtering by level returns only matching tickets; default level on legacy tickets keeps them in ticket set
Regression: non-epic status movement to Implemented remains free and unguarded after epic rules land
MCP: level property present in create_cr and update_cr_attrs schemas, CRAttributes type includes level, handler forwards level, EPIC_* errors surface as JSON-RPC errors

shared TicketService.updateCRStatus: epic to Implemented blocked by non-terminal children (lists them), allowed when all terminal or no children; non-epic unaffected; reopen allowed; existing children not retroactively rejected when epic moves to Proposed
Data-model invariants: no epicId or children[] field introduced (phaseEpic remains the link), and MDT-205 introduces no board card-render flag (epic card exclusion belongs to MDT-206)

Metadata list API (GET /api/projects/:projectId/crs) and the underlying shared getProjectCRsMetadata path preserve level (epic and default ticket) and exclude content; covers both the server integration test and a direct production-path regression so the mock cannot mask a real gap
